issues.description: Default change from EXTERNAL to FIXED silently alters time semantics of who owns end-of-turn
issues.detail: COMPLECTED. The default flip changes which actor decides turn boundaries — a load-bearing time/identity decision — without a migration note for existing callers. Same parameter name, different ownership of 'when does a turn end.' Users upgrading to 0.0.99 will get different conversation timing with no code change. Document the semantic shift loudly, or gate it behind an explicit opt-in.

issues.description: _enable_vad complects 'who detects speech' with 'whether to emit VAD frames' and 'whether to accept external finalize'
issues.detail: PLACE-ORIENTED, COMPLECTED. One boolean now governs three separable concerns: emitting interruption frames, accepting VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame to finalize, and the warning branch. The `elif not self._enable_vad` reads as a double-negative trap. Two named predicates (emits_vad_frames, accepts_external_finalize) derived from the mode enum would decompose this and make the truth table explicit.

issues.description: Warning-then-finalize branch on VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame conflates 'unexpected' with 'ignored'
issues.detail: EASY-NOT-SIMPLE. When `_enable_vad` is true, the code logs a warning and does nothing; when false, it finalizes. The warning suggests the frame is wrong, but the frame is a value — its meaning shouldn't depend on hidden mode state to decide log-vs-act. Either accept-and-finalize unconditionally, or route the frame at the dispatcher so this method only sees frames it should act on.

issues.description: split_sentences threaded through a stringly-typed allowlist instead of as data
issues.detail: INCIDENTAL-COMPLEXITY. Adding a parameter requires editing a name in a hard-coded list and trusting `hasattr` to silently drop typos. The config mapping is data — express it as data (a dict or a derived list from the InputParams schema) so adding a field is one place, not two, and typos surface loudly rather than silently no-op.

issues.description: speech_segment_config always overwritten, even when split_sentences is None
issues.detail: PLACE-ORIENTED. `params.split_sentences or False` collapses None and False into the same write, unconditionally constructing a SpeechSegmentConfig and stomping whatever the SDK default was. If None means 'don't touch,' honor that; if False is the intended default, say so in the schema (`= False`) rather than coercing at the write site.

issues.description: Commented-out start_processing_metrics line moved but not deleted or restored
issues.detail: TDD-AS-DESIGN residue. A commented call was relocated from after the broadcast to before it. Either metrics start at StartOfTurn (uncomment and own it) or they don't (delete the line). Leaving it as a comment encodes an unresolved decision in the source — a value the team hasn't settled, masquerading as code.

review.summary: The change is small but flips a default that owns time semantics — who decides when a turn ends — and routes a different frame type to the same handler. The core complecting is in `_enable_vad`: a single boolean now governs frame emission, external-finalize acceptance, and a warning branch, with a double-negative `elif not self._enable_vad` that should be two named predicates derived from the mode. Config plumbing is stringly-typed and the speech_segment_config write conflates None with False. Decompose the predicates, surface the default-shift in user-facing docs, and either own or delete the relocated commented metrics line.
